newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mt Kersey finds nickel at W.Australia site.
newsitem.headline: Mt Kersey finds nickel at W.Australia site.

text.p: Mt Kersey Mining NL, part of the Joseph Gutnick group, said on Thursday that drilling at the Four Corners project in Western Australia uncovered signs of high grade nickel mineralisation.

The company also said in its June quarter drilling report that it had uncovered low grade gold mineralisation near the Silver Swan nickel mine just north of Kalgoorlie, about 150 km to the southeast of the Four Corners project.
The Silver Swan discovery in November 1995 led to a nickel boom which sent the share price of companies with nearby leases skyrocketting.
The mine is operated by Finland's Outokumpu and privately-held Mining Project Investors Pty Ltd.

Mt Kersey said the latest drilling at Four Corners had recovered 30 metres at 0.67 percent nickel from 74 metres, 28 metres at 0.5 percent nickel from 140 metres and 14 metres at 0.6 percent nickel from 78 metres.
It said the latter recovery was from drilling about 900 metres to the north of the town of Cullens.
"This mineralisation is well above the basal contact and may indicate potential for massive high grade nickel sulphide at the basal contact," it said.
The main focus of drilling at the Gindalbie leases adjacent to Silver Swan was to find extensions or repetitions of the Silver Swan mineralisation.
It said samples had been submitted for assay and added that the project area was also prospective for gold with exploration to the west and southeast of Silver Swan during the latest quarter.

"Shallow low grade oxide gold mineralisation at East Sampson Dam west of Silver Swan has been outlined over a three kilometre strike on a north-north-west trend. The mineralisation occurs over a width of 200 metres."
